Nothing is stored on that path: the throw comes before the writeResource at draft.ts:3096. The new published field holds a version string only (extensions/lib/records.ts:124). GlobalArgsSchema is unchanged. Round 2, judged again for the changed result and round methods. No console call was added; ci.ts logs nothing and is pure. Round 1's smaller gap (a failed dry run left nothing in the log or the blocker) is closed for the user: the thrown blocker now carries swamp's exit code and the end of its stderr (draft.ts:2993-3000), though still no logger call records it. round still logs its start and its decision with named properties (draft.ts:2921, :3087). Smaller gap, new: result logs nothing about the second record it now writes. When it records the published version on the review rounds (draft.ts:2606-2617) no line says so, and when there is no rounds record it skips the write without a word, so the log cannot show whether the next build's count was moved. One info line with name and version would do.

Round 1 finding 1 (round dropped the dry run's exit code and stderr): fixed. round keeps the whole result and, when no content hash was read, adds failure(push, pushed) to the blockers (draft.ts:2983-3000). The test at extensions/models/draft_round_test.ts:515 gives a push that exits 1 with {"status":"failed"} on stdout and the reason on stderr, the shape I saw from real swamp in a scratch copy (a manifest naming a missing model: exit 1, the reason only on stderr), and asserts both 'swamp extension push exited 1' and the reason; with the shipped code put back to a4e52a1 it fails (reproduced: 5 of the changed tests fail there, this one with only 'The publish dry run gave no content hash.'). The text reaches the user redacted (see credentials-secrets). Exit 0 with no hash, reproduced: 'The publish dry run gave no content hash. | swamp extension push exited 0: <end of stdout>', and with empty stdout 'gave no JSON to read. | swamp extension push exited 0'. Odd wording, but nothing is hidden. Round 1 finding 2 (newCommits' git had no timeout): fixed, with one smaller gap. The call now has stdin null and a 60 s abort signal (draft.ts:1449-1453). When the signal fires nothing throws: Deno kills git and output() resolves with code 143 and empty stderr (checked on deno 2.9.7). Reproduced in a scratch copy with the timeout shortened and a git that sleeps: newCommits returns {error: 'git rev-parse failed'} (draft.ts:1466), which visibility shows as 'the new commits could not be read, so their addresses were not checked: git rev-parse failed' and fails the emails check (extensions/lib/visibility.ts:404-416). So it is caught and fails closed, not an unexplained abort, but the message does not say git was given up on after 60 s. When only the origin ref probes time out (draft.ts:1468-1475) the non-zero code is read as 'no such ref', so every commit on HEAD is listed after two minutes with no error; that also errs towards checking more. To fix: treat out.signal !== null as its own error, 'git gave no answer in 60 s'. I judged this a smaller gap because rev-parse and log are local and take no stdin, so I could name no real case that reaches it. Other smaller gaps, new: ciInput returns '' for a ci.yml that is not YAML with no word to the caller (extensions/lib/ci.ts:21-25), so round then blocks on warnings ci.yml accepts and readiness runs the tests with no permissions, neither saying ci.yml could not be read; and failure() keeps only the last 500 characters of stderr (recipe_check.ts:126), while real swamp puts the cause first and repeats the checkout path three times (356 bytes in my run), so a long checkout path can cut the cause off.

Round 1 finding A (a result with no published version erased where the last build ended): fixed. The version last published is now kept on the review-rounds record (extensions/lib/records.ts:119-124); result writes it there when publishedVersion is given (draft.ts:2603-2617), and round and readiness read it from there (draft.ts:3004-3006, :3189-3193). Both writers of that record keep the field: result spreads the parsed record, and round writes it back whether or not it adds a round (draft.ts:3103). The test at draft_round_test.ts:475 does two rounds, a publish through the result method, a new version, a result with nothing published, then expects review 1, review 2 and a refused third; on a4e52a1's code it fails with 'Round 3 would pass the limit'. Probed: result with publishedVersion and no rounds record returns one handle and writes no rounds record, and the next round is review 1, which is right because there are no rounds to count; running result again is safe; a 2026.11.11.1 store has no review-rounds record and the field is optional, so old data reads. If the second write fails after the build result is written, running result again repairs it. Round 1 finding B (#144, finishing a stopped revise wrote no files): fixed. The finishing path now writes spec/app-spec.json again (draft.ts:2749-2770) through the same checkOutputPath as the other writes (draft.ts:2767). It rebuilds the file from what is on disk, so a rerun changes only outOfScope, the recipe phrases and source, as the first run did, and never touches the change plan or the outcome spec. The test at draft_revise_test.ts:299 puts the old app spec back after a stopped run and fails on a4e52a1's code. The log line still says 'whose files the last run wrote' (draft.ts:2774), which is now not quite true. Round 1 finding C (smaller): still present, unchanged. After a refused third round, committing a complete hand-written report makes round record 'committed 0' with no grant (draft.ts:3031-3036; reproduced again: 'committed 0 granted false'), so the limit can be passed without the user's yes. The README and the method description state that a committed complete report needs no round, and a test holds it, so I read it as a known trade-off, not a defect of this change; to close it, refuse 'committed' when the build already has ROUND_LIMIT reviews. Same kind, also not new: result takes publishedVersion on trust, so a result naming the version under review restarts the count (reproduced: review 1, not granted, after a refused round 3); the old code read the same value from the build result.

Round 1 finding B (acceptedWarnings took the next line for an empty value and misread block scalars): fixed. It now reads the job's input from parsed YAML (extensions/lib/rounds.ts:82-84, extensions/lib/ci.ts:19-31); the test at extensions/lib/rounds_test.ts:108 fails on a4e52a1's code. Round 1 finding A (#147, testPermissions misread the tests line and dropped short flags): partly fixed, and this is the issue. What is fixed: a job named tests is no longer taken for the command, a quoted or folded value is read whole, and -R, -W, -N, -E, -S and -I carry over with or without a value (extensions/lib/evidence.ts:139, :147-149; test at extensions/lib/evidence_test.ts:93 fails on a4e52a1's code). What is wrong, both reproduced in a scratch copy: (1) PERMISSION accepts one letter only, so the combined form Deno 2 takes is dropped: `tests: deno test -RW extensions/` gives no flags (deno 2.9.7 runs `deno test -RW` and `-RWN=x` and grants them), and -P / --permission-set is dropped too. readiness then runs the app's tests with no permissions (evidence.ts:176-181), they fail, and it blocks on tests that pass in CI with nothing naming the dropped flag: the #147 failure for another spelling. (2) New with this change: any word of the tests value that looks like a short flag carries over, whichever command it belongs to. `tests: grep -R -E foo . && cp -R a b && ls -S && deno test extensions/` gives ["-R","-E","-R","-S"], so the readiness run gets read, env and sys access that CI's `deno test` does not have, and a test CI would fail for want of permission passes here. The old pattern let only -A and --allow-/--deny- words through, which other tools rarely use; -R, -E, -S and -I are everyday flags of grep, cp, ls and sed. It needs a compound tests command, so it is narrow. To fix: accept -[RWNESI]+(=\S+)? for combined flags, and take flags only from the words of the `deno test` command itself (from 'deno test' up to the next &&, ||, ; or |), or say in the app README that tests must be one deno test command. Smaller, new, reproduced: ciInput returns the first job in file order that gives the input a string (ci.ts:26-29), not the publish job, though the comments at evidence.ts:143-146 and rounds.ts:78-80 say 'the publish job'. With another reusable-workflow job above publish that also takes tests or accepted-warnings, the other job's value wins (two jobs gave ["-A"] and ["env-read"] where publish said --allow-read and deno-command), and a first job whose value is '' stops the search. A rendered ci.yml has one such job (draft.ts:788-799), so this needs a hand-edited ci.yml; prefer the job whose `uses` is puddle-tooling's publish.yml. Checked and sound: a number, boolean, list or missing value gives '', anchors, aliases and merge keys resolve, CRLF reads, and malformed or multi-document YAML gives '' so both callers fall back to no permissions and no accepted warnings. jsr:@std/yaml@1.0.12 is pinned (ci.ts:6), is in deno.lock:9 and :33, and non-test code already imports it (draft.ts:39, readiness.ts:13, visibility.ts:14), so the published bundle needs nothing new. Round 1's smaller gaps: versionDrift now named in the upgrade note, fixed (draft.ts:2086-2087); lastPublished's cast is gone, the value now comes from the rounds record through ReviewRoundsSchema.safeParse, fixed (draft.ts:1785-1794); `git status --porcelain` lines still read with slice(3) (draft.ts:2950), still present, and it only ever calls more paths dirty; #150 (the build result carries one recipe, publishedRecipe at draft.ts:1586) still present and tracked, untouched.
